title: The 20 Percent Plan Disappeared in One Day. Oil Prices Move to the Next Act
part1:
It was as if, on a stage that had just opened, the sign over the theater had been replaced the next day.

The first act was July 13. Mr. Trump posted that he would seek a 20 percent payment from all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The idea was to get back the money the United States spends to keep the strait safe.

However, he did not say who would collect the money, who would pay it, or how it would be calculated. It was not a fee that had actually begun. It was still only a proposal without a detailed system.
part2:
On this day, Brent crude futures moved sharply, as if another act were taking place at the same time. They rose by $7.29, or 9.59 percent, and settled at $83.30 a barrel. Reuters linked the rise to a US sea blockade of Iran that was expected to begin the next day, as well as concerns about energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

In other words, the only thing appearing in this scene was not the 20 percent plan. Tensions over the strait were also on the same stage.

The second act was the next day, July 14. Mr. Trump posted that he was withdrawing the fee plan and replacing the 20 percent with trade and investment deals between the Gulf states and the United States. He also told reporters that no one should charge ships passing through the strait, and that he did not like the idea of fees itself. The plan announced the day before had changed into a different form the next day.
part3:
The market then added a small twist. After the withdrawal was announced, Brent temporarily reduced its gains. But before long, it returned to a high level close to where it had been before the announcement. At the time the article was published, it was up about 2.6 percent and above $85 a barrel. Its settlement price that day was also $84.73, up 1.7 percent from the previous day.

Of course, this alone does not allow us to say for sure what effect the withdrawal had. Concerns continued about the sea blockade, attacks by the United States and Iran, and the safety of tankers.

The main point of these two days is not only that the fee plan appeared and disappeared. Even after the plan left the stage, other concerns over the strait remained. Although it is a distant sea, events in a key route for energy shipments show up in international crude oil prices. The market's stage has not closed yet.
in_one_line: Trump’s proposed 20 percent Strait of Hormuz fee vanished, but tensions there kept oil prices high.
